notes: Compiler declaration/callable inventory now exposes stable identities and typed signature material. A generic reflective invocation boundary for arbitrary callable identities with heterogeneous signatures is still absent, so mncs-test retains a transparent generated binding adapter.

reproducer.actual: mncs-test/tools/generate_provider.py consumes mncs declaration-inventory and emits provider_inventory.mncs because provider.mncs cannot yet invoke a callable by identity with heterogeneous typed arguments.
reproducer.expected: A generic runtime/MNCS binding accepts an authoritative callable identity plus typed invocation material, preserving declaration, function, test-case, source, and profile identities without consumer-specific dispatch generation.

requiredBehavior: Expose a bounded generic typed invocation surface for an inventory callable identity, with signature validation, exported-surface admission, source/profile identity binding, and fail-closed mismatch behavior.
summary: The compiler-owned inventory removes repository inference and test-name scraping, but the language/runtime cannot yet dynamically bind and invoke arbitrary heterogeneous callable identities. The remaining generator is transparent typed glue rather than a semantic test registry.
title: Generic callable inventory lacks reflective typed invocation binding
